newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries bounce from early weakness, end flat.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries bounce from early weakness, end flat.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries recovered from early weakness to close largely unchanged on Thursday, with much of the market sidelined ahead of Friday's producer price index (PPI) report.
The 30-year bond ended at 100-25/32, unchanged, to yield 6.56 percent.
"We are stuck in this range," said one head trader at a primary dealership. "I don't know if PPI matters, but it might break us out of the range."
Short-covering and a large buyer of 10-year note futures aided the market's ascent, market participants said.
Activity was described as very light, with volume at about $65 billion, according to GovPX.
"People are pretty much squared away for tomorrow (PPI)," Nealis said.
The PPI is expected to have been unchanged in June, with core PPI seen up 0.1 percent in June, a Reuters poll shows.
Earlier on Thursday, the market shrugged off a huge rise in jobless claims to 377,000 in the week ended July 5 from 337,000 the prior week. Economists dismissed the gain as a quirk.

In late trading, the two-year note was unchanged at 100-6/32 to yield 5.90 percent. The five-year note was up 1/32 at 100-14/32 with a yield of 6.15 percent. The 10-year note closed unchanged at 102-22/32 to yield 6.25 percent.
The three-month bill was up six basis points to 5.03 percent. The six-month bill was up two basis points at 5.10 percent and the year-bill was down one basis point at 5.23 percent.
